hardware_scope: macOS host and Linux virtual machine ran on one Apple M3. This measures cross-OS readability on arm64.

positive_checks_per_os.success: Every CLI unpack produced the exact original bytes. Archive and original SHA-256 were checked before unpack. Both systems used the same set of archives. The two v0.2 presets selected identical bytes on eight inputs.

negative_checks_per_os.covered: Headers, truncation, trailing bytes, altered checksums, sizes, dictionary stream and index errors, concatenated XZ, expansion limits and reserved Brotli large-window headers.
negative_checks_per_os.destination: Every failed unpack --force returned an error and preserved an existing output byte-for-byte.

other_checks.selector_fallback: With Brotli hidden, optional packing selected dictionary-xz on A1_RECT_cassette.step. Inputs containing the four reserved bytes individually fell back to CNF1 and restored exactly.

linux_encoded_macos_decoded.success: All three Linux-encoded frames were additionally transferred to macOS and restored to the exact original bytes.

repeat_public_checks.from: Release repository root, with Python 3 and the brotli executable on PATH to exercise optional profiles.
repeat_public_checks.fixture_scope: preview/test_preview.py and preview/test_sxd3.py exercise shipped historical fixtures, corruption handling and optional-method behavior. These runnable regressions are a smaller suite than the two-OS study above.
